meta.location: The wilderness, then the land of Nephi
meta.date: ~588–559 BC (the separation, to forty years out)

world_behind.title: The founding gesture repeats
world_behind.text: Lehi fled Jerusalem on a dream-warning; his son now flees his brothers on the same authority: "the Lord did warn me, that I, Nephi, should depart from them and flee into the wilderness" (v. 5). This family's covenant history moves by departures, and the record makes the parallel unmistakable: tents taken, a journey of "many days" (v. 7), a new land pitched and named.

world_behind.title: A people named for a man
world_behind.text: "Did take upon them to call themselves the people of Nephi" (v. 9): identity in the new colony runs by covenant leader. The record will keep the convention for centuries: Nephites and Lamanites are names a person takes on, and later chapters can move individuals between them.

world_behind.title: An exile temple was thinkable
world_behind.text: A sanctuary "after the manner of the temple of Solomon" (v. 16), scaled to available materials, built far from Jerusalem: the era offers a real parallel in the Jewish temple at Elephantine in Egypt, raised by another displaced community in these same decades. Exiles who took the covenant seriously built for it.

cites.quote: after the manner of the temple of Solomon

spans.text: after the manner of the temple of Solomon

world_behind.title: No king, on principle
world_behind.text: "I, Nephi, was desirous that they should have no king" (v. 18): the founder declines the era's default institution, a rare position in an age when every neighboring people organized under monarchy. The stance is remembered: when Mosiah finally dismantles Nephite kingship centuries later (Mosiah 29), he is arguing what Nephi here enacts.

world_behind.title: The cursing, in the text's own terms
world_behind.text: The record defines the cursing at verse 20 in covenant language: "they were cut off from his presence" (v. 20), the exact penalty spoken in the valley (1 Ne. 2:21). The mark of verse 21 is described as separation mechanics with repentance as its exit ("save they shall repent of their iniquities" (v. 22)), and the record itself will push back on any contempt built on it: all are alike unto God (2 Ne. 26:33), and Jacob will turn the comparison against Nephite pride outright (Jacob 3:9).

world_behind.title: A decade in two notices
world_behind.text: Thirty years out, the small plates are commanded (v. 30); forty years out, wars have begun (v. 34). Everything the reader has read so far was engraved from this vantage: the whole record of 1 Nephi is a thirty-years-later work of memory, which explains its shaped, thematic telling.

words.text: The command is to leave the brethren behind: "flee into the wilderness" (v. 5). Flight in this record is an obedience word, not a coward's: Lehi fled, Nephi flees, and this second flight follows an attempt on Nephi's life (v. 2). Some situations are answered faithfully only by leaving.

cites.quote: flee into the wilderness

spans.text: flee into the wilderness

words.text: In King James English the word belongs to weapons: a bow of steel broken in the arms (2 Sam. 22:35), the northern iron and the steel (Jer. 15:12). This family's two encounters with it run the same way, Laban's blade (1 Ne. 4:9) and the bow that snapped in the wilderness (1 Ne. 16:18). Here it turns up in a shop list, "wood, and of iron, and of copper, and of brass, and of steel" (v. 15), taught to a whole colony next to carpentry. What had been the metal of the family's worst moments becomes a trade.

words.text: The way a thing is put together. The word appears once in this record and never in the King James Bible, and Nephi uses it to draw a careful line. The temple could not be built of so many precious things, since the materials were not on the land, and yet "the manner of the construction was like unto the temple of Solomon" (v. 16). What carried over was the plan.

words.text: "Did cause my people to be industrious, and to labor with their hands" (v. 17): the colony's founding economics, stated as a commandment kept. The record treats industry as a spiritual datum, listed between temple-building and kingship; idleness will appear one verse later as a mark of the cursed condition (v. 24), and the contrast is deliberate.

words.text: Third use in five chapters: land (2 Ne. 1:7), afflictions (2 Ne. 2:2), and now persons, Jacob and Joseph "that they should be priests and teachers over the land of my people" (v. 26). The verb's arc is the colony's: everything the covenant touches, territory, suffering, and finally ministry, gets set apart for sacred use.

words.text: An engraver's word for stopping. Treated at 1 Nephi 6:2. Forty years and a war close the book in a single line because the writer judges that enough: "it sufficeth me to say that forty years had passed away, and we had already had wars and contentions with our brethren" (v. 34). The formula runs in the family trade. Nephi used it to skip the genealogy (1 Ne. 6:2), Jarom uses it to explain why he writes so little (Jarom 1:2), and Moroni to hold back most of what the brother of Jared saw (Ether 3:17). It marks the spot where the keeper of the plates sets the limit, rather than the material setting it.

phrases.term: All those who would go with me
phrases.text: The migration's membership clause, stated twice and then defined: "those who believed in the warnings and the revelations of God" (v. 6). The split does not run along bloodlines, Zoram's house, Sam's, sisters, and unnamed others cross it, but along belief. The first Nephite community is a church before it is an ethnicity.

phrases.text: The covenant formula's bright clause, executing on schedule and flagged again two verses later ("began to prosper exceedingly" (v. 13)). Sown seed, reaped abundance, flocks and herds: the record submits its evidence that the valley promise (1 Ne. 2:20; 2 Ne. 1:20) pays as written, before showing the dark clause executing too.

phrases.term: After the manner of the temple of Solomon
phrases.text: The pattern named, the scale conceded: not "built of so many precious things" (v. 16), for "they were not to be found upon the land" (v. 16). The record's honesty about the downgrade is the point: covenant worship replicates the pattern, not the budget, and the appraiser's formula still applies to the result.

phrases.term: They would that I should be their king
phrases.text: The offer the whole quarrel predicted, made at last by the willing, and declined by the accused. The brothers murdered sleep over a kingship Nephi refuses when it is freely given; the record lets the irony stand without comment, and adds only what he did instead: "I did for them according to that which was in my power" (v. 18).

cites.quote: I did for them according to that which was in my power

spans.text: I did for them according to that which was in my power

phrases.text: The record's most quoted five words about community, placed with terrible care: after a murder plot, a family rupture, and a cursing. Happiness here is a manner, a practiced way, law kept, hands laboring, a temple standing, records kept, not a circumstance; the chapter is its recipe as much as its report.

The commandment that created the book in the reader's hands. Thirty years of history already lay on the large plates; the Lord orders a second engraving "for the profit of thy people" (v. 30), and Nephi obeys without knowing the wise purpose (1 Ne. 9:5). Every chapter read so far is the fruit of this verse.

cites.quote: for the profit of thy people

spans.text: for the profit of thy people

verses.label: v. 6
verses.title: A roster that finally admits the sisters
verses.text: The departure list names Nephi's family, Zoram and his family, Sam and his, Jacob and Joseph, "and also my sisters, and all those who would go with me." This is the first mention of sisters in the record. The comparable roster at 1 Nephi 2:5 named mother and brothers only. They arrive here without names, without a number, and without explanation for the earlier silence, and the record never returns to them.

verses.label: v. 14
verses.title: A single artifact turned into a pattern
verses.text: The record reports the sword of Laban being used as a template: "after the manner of it did make many swords." The weapon taken at 1 Nephi 4:9 becomes the specification for an armory. The stated reason follows in the same verse and is precise about its grounds, "for I knew their hatred towards me and my children," so what the record gives as the cause of the rearmament is a personal knowledge rather than a general threat.

verses.label: v. 18–20
verses.title: A crown refused and a function kept
verses.text: The record separates two things a reader might merge. The people ask for a king and the request is declined: "I, Nephi, was desirous that they should have no king." One verse later the same man reports holding a different office, "I should be their ruler and their teacher," and states that it fulfils a promise made at 1 Nephi 2:22. The record thus has him decline the title he was offered and retain the role he was given, and verse 20 completes the pair by reporting the other half of that same promise fulfilled as well.

verses.label: v. 28–34
verses.title: Two dates with a commandment between them
verses.text: The record gives a year at verse 28, "thirty years had passed away from the time we left Jerusalem," and another at verse 34, "forty years had passed away." Between the two sits the order to make a second set of plates and the making of them, so the whole small-plates project is placed inside a ten-year window and is dated from an event on another continent. Verse 33 also sends the reader elsewhere for the omitted material, "they must search mine other plates," which is the same division of labor announced at 1 Nephi 9:2–4.

chapter.title: The valley's words execute in full
chapter.text: Prosper-exceedingly lands at verse 11; cut-off-from-presence lands at verse 20; ruler-and-teacher at verse 19; the scourge clause at verse 25. The chapter is 1 Nephi 2 fulfilled line by line, and the record flags each landing explicitly: prophecy in this book is checkable, and it checks.

chapter.title: The split is grieved
chapter.text: The chapter opens with Nephi crying to the Lord and closes with wars; between them the separation is executed as commanded but never gloated. The record's founding schism is a failure of the family's oldest hope, and the writer who lived it lets the sorrow show at both edges.

chapter.title: A civilization in one chapter
chapter.text: Eight institutions are established between verses 10 and 31: the law of Moses kept, sowing and reaping, swords made after the pattern of Laban's, work "in all manner of wood, and of iron, and of copper, and of brass, and of steel, and of gold, and of silver," a temple, a refused kingship, Jacob and Joseph consecrated priests and teachers, and a second set of plates. Verse 27 sums the result in six words, "we lived after the manner of happiness." The same inventory recurs at Alma 1:26–29 and 4 Nephi 1:2–3 as the description of a working society.

chapter.title: The record keeps its own conscience
chapter.text: Verses 21 through 24 are kept without softening, and so is the limit attached to them at verse 22, "save they shall repent of their iniquities." The record then prints its own corrections elsewhere: Jacob 3:5–9 rebukes the Nephites for despising the other people, Alma 9:15–17 says it will be "more tolerable for them in the day of judgment than for you," and Alma 17:15 attributes their state to "the traditions of their fathers." The hardest sentences and the later rebukes of those who quote them stand in the same volume.

chapter.title: Authority is what you do, not what you wear
chapter.text: Nephi rules as the Lord commanded, declines the crown, and defines his office as doing "according to that which was in my power" (v. 18). The brothers wanted rule as inheritance; the record shows it as labor, and the difference is the whole quarrel.

cites.quote: according to that which was in my power

spans.text: according to that which was in my power

chapter.title: Happiness is a manner
chapter.text: Verse 27's placement is the doctrine: after rupture, amid threat, before wars. The record locates happiness in the practiced shape of covenant life, which means it was available the whole time, and remains so.

chapter.title: The book explains its own birth
chapter.text: Verse 30 is where the small plates begin; the reader has been holding this chapter's consequence since page one. The record's structure is now visible: a thirty-years-later act of obedience, engraving what is pleasing to God out of a history that included this chapter's grief.

applications.title: Leave what seeks your life
applications.text: Some environments are dangers to depart: the warning to flee is as much revelation as the command to stay. If a situation is destroying you, pray Nephi's prayer and take seriously that the answer may be departure, with everyone who will come.

applications.title: Take everyone who believes
applications.text: When you build your next community, a home, a ward effort, a venture, draw its line where Nephi drew his: belief and willingness. Zoram and the sisters crossed; so can the unexpected people in your life.

applications.title: Build the temple you can afford
applications.text: Do not postpone worship until resources match Solomon. Build now, after the pattern, at your scale: the family altar, the modest practice, the small consistent observance. The formula judges workmanship, whatever the materials.

applications.title: Serve without the crown
applications.text: Where you hold real influence, practice Nephi's refusal: do according to what is in your power and decline the title that would make it about you. Authority declined and service rendered is the chapter's model of greatness.

applications.title: Run the happiness recipe
applications.text: Audit your household against the chapter's manner: commandments kept, hands laboring at something real, worship built and attended, a record being written. Happiness in this pattern is infrastructure; check which piece is missing before blaming circumstances.

applications.title: Consecrate the young ones
applications.text: Jacob and Joseph were the family's youngest and its future ministry. Find the rising generation in your circle and give them consecrated responsibility, real callings with real trust, before the need is desperate.

questions.text: What am I currently only crying to the Lord about that may require the obedience of departure?
Which abuses am I still archiving in detail that my soul-track would be healthier refusing to record?
Where have I postponed building worship because the materials fall short of the pattern I remember?
Which crown is currently on offer in my life, and what would declining it in favor of the work actually look like?
What scourge in my own story might be functioning to stir me up in remembrance, and is it working?
If a stranger audited my week, would they find a manner of happiness or a wait for circumstances?
